title: When the House Wakes
premise: Orsen Crane returns to the family house in Frost Hollow to bury their twin brother Aldous, only to find that no one in town remembers which twin died—or that there were ever two. Waiting on the porch is Wren, the imaginary friend from childhood, unchanged after twenty years, who insists Orsen was the one who was invited into the world and Aldous was the one left outside. As frost patterns spread across the windows spelling out names, Orsen must survive one night inside the waking house, learning that their parents made a bargain to swap which child belonged to this world—and the debt has come due at sunrise.
about_author: Emrys Winterbourne is the pen name of a former archivist of New England estate records who spent a decade cataloguing houses that outlived their families. They write horror about inheritance, believing every home keeps a ledger of what it is owed.

chapters.title: The Wrong Sibling
chapters.summary: Orsen arrives in Frost Hollow by bus at dusk, carrying Aldous's ashes, and finds the funeral notice bears their own name. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: disorientation and grief tangled with the eerie sense of being erased.

chapters.title: Porch Light
chapters.summary: At the house, every light burns though the power was cut years ago. On the porch sits Wren—unchanged since childhood—who greets Orsen by name and says, 'You came back to the wrong door.' POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: dread sharpened by unwanted nostalgia.

chapters.title: Inventory
chapters.summary: Orsen counts the doors as they always did—eleven inside, twelve at midnight—and catalogs the house's impossible changes: rooms wider, hallways longer, a nursery that shouldn't exist. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: the compulsion of old rituals as armor against fear.

chapters.title: What the Town Remembers
chapters.summary: Orsen visits the diner; the locals offer condolences for 'the Crane child' but cannot say which one died, and the undertaker's ledger shows two graves already dug. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: isolation deepening—the town itself is complicit or enchanted.

chapters.title: Wren's Terms
chapters.summary: Wren explains the rules: stay until sunrise, keep the lights on, answer no knock before dawn, and never say both twins' names aloud in the same room. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance with something not human.

chapters.title: The Nursery That Grew
chapters.summary: Orsen finds the nursery furnished with two cribs, one scorched, one pristine, and a wall of frost forming a pattern like a door. Flashbacks reveal childhood games with Wren that were never games. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: memory turning traitorous.

chapters.title: Aldous's Letters
chapters.summary: In the attic, Orsen discovers letters in Aldous's handwriting, dated after his death, describing 'the cold side of the glass' and begging Orsen not to open the frost door. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: hope curdling into horror.

chapters.title: The Knocking
chapters.summary: Night falls fully. Something knocks at every door in sequence, patient and polite, using Aldous's voice, then their mother's. Orsen counts doors to stay sane. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: terror disciplined by ritual.

chapters.title: Mother's Ledger
chapters.summary: Orsen finds their mother's journal: a bargain struck with 'the landlord of the frost' when the twins were born—one child for this world, one held in reserve. The entry naming which twin was given is torn out. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: betrayal across generations.

chapters.title: Wren's True Face
chapters.summary: Pressed on what Wren is, the friend's shape flickers—tall, jointed, patient—and admits it was the thing the parents bargained with, wearing a child's invention as a mask. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: the loss of the last safe thing.

chapters.title: The Neighbor Who Waited
chapters.summary: Mrs. Halloway, ancient neighbor, reveals she buried a twin too, sixty years ago, and warns Orsen: the house doesn't collect debts, it collects identities. She refuses to cross the property line. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: confirmation that this is a cycle.

chapters.title: Frost Writing
chapters.summary: The windows frost over from the inside, letters forming: first ALDOUS, then ORSEN, then a third name scraped away. The house is deciding whom it holds. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: identity dissolving under supernatural pressure.

chapters.title: The Second Grave
chapters.summary: Defying Wren, Orsen digs at the family plot and opens the second prepared grave: empty except for a mirror, fogged, warm to the touch. Their reflection moves independently. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: confronting the possibility they are the one who died.

chapters.title: Which Twin Came Home
chapters.summary: Memories fracture—two childhoods overlapping, each remembered from both sides. Wren gently suggests Orsen has been the one behind the glass all along, and Aldous lived the borrowed life. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: identity crisis at its nadir.

chapters.title: Doors Thirteen
chapters.summary: The house grows a thirteenth door. Behind it: the nursery again, but occupied—a figure shaped like Orsen, waiting, patient as frost. It speaks with Orsen's voice. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: facing the self that was traded away.

chapters.title: The Bargain Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Orsen reads the full contract found sewn into mother's wedding quilt: the swap can be undone before sunrise if the named heir willingly renounces belonging—but the house will keep whoever remains unclaimed. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: agency reclaimed through terrible knowledge.

chapters.title: What Aldous Wants
chapters.summary: Through the frost glass, Aldous communicates—not vengeful but exhausted, asking only to be remembered or released, not swapped back. Orsen realizes the enemy is the house, not the brother. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: compassion replacing fear.

chapters.title: Renunciation
chapters.summary: Before the thirteenth door, Orsen begins the renunciation, giving up name, inheritance, and place—but Wren intervenes, revealing it wants Orsen claimed so the cycle continues with a new 'imaginary friend' for the next generation. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: climax of will versus design.

chapters.title: Sunrise Clause
chapters.summary: As dawn nears, the house floods with cold light; every door opens at once, and all the previous heirs—Halloways, Cranes—stand in the thresholds, hollow, still keeping their counts. Orsen runs the final hallway. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: desperate sprint through ancestral damnation.

chapters.title: Naming the House
chapters.summary: Climax: at the threshold, Orsen does the forbidden thing—speaks both twins' names together, claiming Aldous as kin rather than payment. The contract, built on division, cannot parse unity; the frost shatters inward. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: love weaponized as loophole.

chapters.title: After the Frost
chapters.summary: Sunrise. The house is ordinary, small, dying. One grave holds ashes, the other the shattered mirror. Wren is gone—or is a child's chalk drawing on the porch boards. Orsen buries Aldous properly, under their own name in error, and lets it stand. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: grief accepted, identity chosen rather than assigned.

chapters.title: Keeping the Lights
chapters.summary: Epilogue: Orsen stays in Frost Hollow, keeper of the house now emptied of its hunger, teaching the next family's children to count doors—for safety, not ritual. Some nights, frost writes a single word on the glass: THANKS. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: belonging finally earned, haunted but chosen.
